svg.desc: Two panels from Morris and Shin's model as Svensson restates it, with a weight of 3/4 on the beauty contest and the private precision fixed at one, against the public precision as a multiple of the private precision from 0 to 2. Top, expected welfare times the private precision: −1 with no public signal (dashed), falling to its lowest value, −4/3, at 1/8, back at −1 at 1/2, −0.68 at 1 and −0.407 at 2. Bottom, the weight on the public signal in equilibrium and the weight Bayes' rule alone would give it: 1/3 against 1/9 at 1/8, 0.8 against 0.5 at 1 and 0.889 against 0.667 at 2. The range of the horizontal axis is this book's choice; Svensson's upward shift of 1.5 is not applied; every number is this book's calculation.
